_summary.verdict: Level-3 trilinear/quadrilinear lift gives a tightening of order 1e-6 vs Lasserre-2 — about 20x smaller than the L2-over-Bochner gap. Implementation is mathematically valid (PSD on bordered moment-matrix lift), but the actual tightening is far smaller than worth pursuing. The Fejér-Riesz / Bochner equivalence for trig nonneg-polys means level-3 only adds NEW info via auxiliary moment lifts on (c_k, d_k), not via level-3 trig localizers. Levels above 2 face strongly diminishing returns for this problem.
_summary.tractability_at_full_problem_size: Proportional to (M3_max * (T_loc3+1)^2) extra real PSD constraints, plus M3_max bordered lifts of size 2L_lift+1 = 2T3_lift+3. At our row-4 default (T_max=30, T_loc=8), we expect L3 cost to add roughly 30s on top of the 37s Lasserre-2 solve at N=10000, T=4000 — feasible but not exciting.
_summary.engineering_recommendation: NOT worth pursuing as currently implemented. The Toeplitz block decomposition works (no SDP blow-up), but the marginal tightening (~1e-6) is below the solver's optimal_inaccurate noise floor at full problem size. A stronger tightening would require either (i) lifting all bilinear products of f̂(j)f̂(k) into an outer (T_max+1)^2-sized variable (intractable), or (ii) finding NEW polynomial constraints on (c_k, d_k) beyond White's (5.13) that benefit from level-3 lift.

config._note_on_size: We attempted SIZE=full (N=2000, T=200, T_max=10) but the run did not complete in budget. The med results below establish: (a) L3 tightens L2 by ~5.9e-7, (b) solve time grew only modestly. The 'full' (production) problem at N=10000, T=4000 should remain tractable since the level-3 constraint cost is independent of N (only of T_max and T3_lift, which we keep small).
